money._basis: GPU actual from the session record plus container disk derived at THIS attempt's own authorization rate, both ceiled to the 4-decimal quantum

what_happened:
FORMAL TRAINING BEGAN AND ONE PROBE WAS COMPLETED. Stages P, S and R passed; stage P rebuilt both arms; stage C trained the eleventh probe of the twelve -- `confirmation.1a2b5b030e7e4e202fda3a810ed53c5f.s1523147638`, the advanced candidate at the third confirmation seed -- announced it durable, and then raised.

probes_trained went 10 -> 11. probes_scored stayed 10. The failure is in `attest`, which runs once per rung after the rung's first probe exists, BEFORE that probe is scored. So the campaign now holds one probe that is trained, durable and not yet scored.
root_cause:
`attest` builds an evaluation package from a real trained checkpoint and took `next(iter(self.training.values()))` to find one. That is safe only while every journal entry holds weights on this pod. Under AGENTS.md P8.4 a completed and validly scored probe is admitted as EVIDENCE -- rows, score, descriptor, hashes, and no `model_dir`, because nothing remaining reads its checkpoint -- so a continuation's journal leads with ten such entries and the call raised `KeyError: 'model_dir'`.

The record shape is mine, introduced with the consumer-derived working set, and I did not trace it to this consumer. `attest` is also a SEAM: every driver fake in the test suite replaces it, so the injected function was the only unexecuted code left on the path -- which is why no test could have caught this.
repair: `attest` now selects, deterministically by sorted key, a journal entry whose `model_dir` exists on this pod, and raises a message naming the evidence-only state if there is none. A test drives the REAL `attest` selection -- the first test in the suite to do so -- with an evidence-only journal, with one local checkpoint among them, and with a restored entry whose recorded path does not exist here, which is what a predecessor's `model_dir` looks like on a replacement resource. Both mutations (back to first-found; ignore whether the path exists) fail it.
the_probe_was_preserved: 2.22 GiB fetched off-pod and RE-IDENTIFIED FROM THE DELIVERED BYTES, with its probe_record.json and a durable_ack.json beside it, before the pod was deleted behind its teardown gate. 62 minutes of formal training survived the failure of a later stage, which is what AGENTS.md requires of expensive completed work.
resume_contract:
This is the state the resume preregistration was written for -- 'an interruption part-way through is likely enough that the reuse question will be asked under time pressure, and that is the worst moment to decide it'. R2 supplies the mechanism: the bytes are restored from the durable destination, re-identified at the new local path before the journal admits them, and `score_existing` scores that checkpoint. R3 and `what_a_resume_may_never_do` forbid the alternative in as many words: a resume may never 'retrain a probe whose checkpoint was restored but whose scoring failed', nor 'rebuild the initialization of a probe that already holds its trained checkpoint', nor 'price a score-only probe as a full training probe'.

So the next attempt does not retrain it. `remaining_work` derives this without intervention: 1 score-only probe, 1 train-and-score probe (incumbent B at the same seed), arms_needed ['B'] alone, and a weights leg of exactly one probe.
what_the_resume_costs: LESS than the pair it replaces, because the candidate's training and its arm are banked: materialization 60.3 -> 30.15 minutes, expected window 339.31 -> 282.38, hard all-in $8.4201 -> $7.2540. The weights reserve returns to 45 minutes from 10, correctly: this campaign finally has a probe whose checkpoint a remaining operation reads.
the_datacenter_pin_returns_and_that_is_c: the weights leg reads from the attached network volume, so probe 11 must be pre-staged there and the draw is pinned to EU-NL-1 again. `volume_attachment` derives that from need and will attach it automatically now that a consumer exists -- which is the amendment-6 repair behaving as designed rather than a regression. Retraining would cost about 75 minutes of L40S against about 54 minutes of $0.06/h CPU staging, so the contract and the cheaper path agree.
regression: the attest selection test plus the full preflight scope; both mutations of the fix fail the new test.
why_a_fresh_chain: the repair is in the driver, an entry point of the executable closure, so the closure moved and attempt12's authorization and bundle no longer bind this tree.
consumed: $2.2614 all-in for 122.61 minutes of L40S. One provider resource, created and provider-confirmed deleted behind its teardown gate. One probe trained, preserved and re-identified; none scored.
